> 聞在宥天下，不聞治天下也。

I have heard of letting the world be, never of governing it.

That sentence is usually taken as a slogan against government. It is finer than that, and it turns on one character.

## 在 and 宥 are one action with two sides

在: to be present, to cause something to rest in its place. 宥: 郭象 glosses 寬也 — wide, yielding, not crowding. 成玄英: 寬宥.

They are not two policies. They are two faces of one thing: room it enough to be as it is (宥), and only then does it settle (在). You cannot make a thing settle first and make room for it afterwards.

## 撄 is the villain, and it is a small word

撄: 手 with 嬰 as phonetic — to touch, to pluck, to disturb. Its base sense is not "teach" and not "order." It is: the hand touches the water, and rings spread.

That is where this chapter's charge lands. Not on the wrong content. On the action: the hand should not have moved.

So the famous line 昔堯之治天下也，使天下欣欣焉人樂其性，是不恬也 is not a complaint about oppression. It is a complaint about success: the ruler made everyone happy about their nature, and that is 不恬 — not still. Delight is as much a movement as pain.

## 毗: the bias attaches

毗: 田 with 比 as phonetic — to lean against, to attach to one side. 大喜毗於陽，大怒毗於陰: once an emotion tips, it attaches, and the balance of yin and yang is gone.

Note the verb. Emotion does not merely appear; it takes a side and holds there.

## 涬溟: back to before the split

涬溟: the undifferentiated haze, the state of heaven and earth before they separated. 鴻蒙 tells 雲將 to be one with it.

This is not nostalgia for chaos. It is the recognition that most of our problems are downstream of a division that was made, and can be unmade — not by solving the halves, but by not standing in one.

## 各復其根, and the three characters that matter

根 is the place a thing returns to. The sentence continues 而不知 — and does not know it.

Three characters do all the work. Return to the root and know that you are returning, and you have started a new project. Return and not know, and it is simply where you are.

## The test

Find one person, team, or thing you are currently "improving." Then check the verb: is it 宥 — room enough to be as it is — or is it 撄 — a hand that touched the water and thinks the rings are the thing's own motion? The chapter says the fault is not in what you wanted. It is in the fact that a hand moved at all.
